chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who buys silver coins from another man, weighs them, and knows their weight, then says to him: 'Keep them with you in their current state until I return to you, and I have the option (to accept or reject) regarding you.' He (the Imam) said: 'If it is with the option, there is no harm in him buying it from him; otherwise, there is no harm.'

key_terms.الْخِيَارِ: The option/right to choose (accept or reject a contract)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy silver coins and leave them with the seller while retaining the right to inspect or cancel the deal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the validity of a conditional sale (*bay' al-khiyar*) of silver coins (*wariq*) where the buyer retains the right to rescind the deal, a common practice in early Islamic commerce to mitigate risk. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that the permissibility hinges on the explicit agreement of this option, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that clarity in contractual terms prevents dispute (*gharar*). This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia commercial law in accommodating practical market needs while maintaining strict adherence to contractual integrity.
